scene.title: GT Track Car — Exploded Systems Study
scene.description: Representative rear-engine two-door GT track car decomposed into aero, body, chassis, powertrain and cockpit systems.

steps.title: The assembled car
steps.caption: A representative rear-engine GT track car: a bonded body-in-white carries the aero, chassis, powertrain and cockpit systems numbered in the legend.

steps.title: Aero package
steps.caption: Splitter, active front flaps, underbody diffusers, CFRP sills and a swan-neck rear wing work as one downforce system.

steps.title: Body panels
steps.caption: Bonnet, fenders, roof and doors are slices of one surface, so they meet seamlessly when assembled.

steps.title: Chassis corners
steps.caption: Double wishbones at the front, multi-link at the rear, carbon-ceramic brakes and forged centre-lock wheels. Detail A magnifies the front-left hub.

steps.title: Powertrain
steps.caption: The flat-six sits behind the rear axle with its plenum on top; the dual-clutch transaxle and drive shafts sit ahead of it, the centre-exit exhaust behind.

steps.title: Cockpit and safety cell
steps.caption: Bucket seats, dashboard module and the bolted roll cage.

steps.title: As a publication drawing
steps.caption: The same scene as vector line art with balloons and the systems legend — export it as SVG, a drawing sheet or a journal figure.

metadata.author: spatial-diagram skill
metadata.notes: Representative geometry inspired by a user-supplied exploded systems poster of a rear-engine GT track car. Generic, unbranded vehicle: proportions approximate a 4.57 m two-door coupé; no OEM model, part numbers, mass or performance claims. Body panels are superellipse lofts; vents, glazing seals, fasteners, wiring, fuel and hydraulic systems are omitted or symbolic. Exploding bonded and welded structure explains packaging, not a service procedure.
